text:
Thursday's comeback against Buffalo had Frank Nazar's fingerprints all over it: two goals, five shots, and a tip of Rinzel's point shot to tie the game before Ryan Donato won it in overtime. "We worked hard and we earned it," he said afterward, in the Blackhawks' postgame video. The Athletic's Scott Powers had a sharper read during the game, posting that the Moore, Nazar and Kane line was "the only one creating anything for the Blackhawks."

That's the season in a sentence. Nazar has 7 goals in 17 games and is scoring on 21% of his shots, well above our range for him, so some of the goals will dry up. The assists are the opposite story. Chicago has scored 10.7 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that is why he has only two helpers.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 62% of his entries last season. Watch the points: the goals may slow, but the assists should start arriving.
